page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.medium is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine designed for basic operational workloads. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor (x86_64 architecture) provisioned with 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs via hyper-threading. The instance includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache, with instruction set support including AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. Memory capacity is set at 8.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation. The server provides no bundled local storage and contains zero GPUs, necessitating external network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance consistently in entry-tier percentiles. In stress-ng evaluations, the single-core score recorded 1107.09 and multi-core score registered 2193.58, reflecting bottom-quartile throughput. PassMark testing mirrors these findings with an aggregate CPU score of 2641.62 and memory score of 1211.79. Memory bandwidth reaches 157.12 GB/sec for small cached 16 KB read blocks, but drops to 16.61 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 14.38 GB/sec on writes. Synthetic application benchmarks show static web serving throughput at 1.69 GB/sec, single-threaded gzip compression at 18.98 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput at 2.49 million operations per second.

Given the limited multi-core processing capacity and absence of ephemeral local storage, this configuration is cost-efficient primarily for non-intensive compute tasks where baseline memory capacity is required. Appropriate use cases encompass dev/test environments, microservices, lightweight web servers, basic CI/CD utility nodes, and small low-concurrency Redis caching layers. Workloads with heavy data processing, high thread contention, or intensive I/O requirements require larger instance tiers with additional physical cores.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.medium is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 2 vCPUs on a single physical core via an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 support, it is paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance provisions no onboard local storage and contains zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations indicate entry-tier performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 2641.62, multi-core stress-ng score of 2193.58, uncached memory read bandwidth of 16.61 GB/sec, and Redis throughput of 2.49 million operations per second. Its qualitative cost efficiency is oriented toward low-utilization scenarios where dedicated core allocation is secondary. Best-fit workloads include development and test environments, small web servers, auxiliary microservices, and lightweight caching layers.
